subject: Ruth
note: Evidence for Ruth's Bible figure page. A short record (the book of Ruth, 85 verses, and Matthew 1:5), so a short page: seven moments (the book's own scenes), no miracles, no death section (Scripture says nothing of her end; the Hebron tomb is a fact under 'Died', named as a place shown to travellers). No personality type. Every quotation is in ruth.quotes.json and passes verify-quotes.mjs. Bible lines are from the Berean Standard Bible (shared/bsb-berean-standard-bible.txt). Fetched texts are in design/saints-hub/sources/people/ruth/ (gitignored). Rahab's page is written at the same time: Matthew 1:5 names both; this page links her in 'Friends, family and rivals' as the mother of Boaz.

life.text: In the days when the judges ruled, a famine drove Elimelech of Bethlehem, his wife Naomi and their sons Mahlon and Chilion to Moab; Elimelech died; the sons married Moabite women, Orpah and Ruth; after about ten years both sons died.
life.source: Ruth 1:1-5 (BSB).

life.text: Ruth's first husband was Mahlon (named only at Ruth 4:10).
life.source: Ruth 4:10 (BSB): "I have acquired Ruth the Moabitess, Mahlon's widow, as my wife". Josephus, Antiquities 5.9.1, agrees ("Ruth for Mahlon").

life.text: On the road Naomi urged both daughters-in-law to go home; Orpah kissed her goodbye; Ruth clung to her and made her vow (1:16-17); Naomi stopped persuading her.
life.source: Ruth 1:6-18 (BSB).
life.note: 'Naomi heard that the LORD had given His people food again' paraphrases 1:6, 'the LORD had attended to His people by providing them with food'.

life.text: At Bethlehem the town was stirred; Naomi said 'Call me Mara'; they arrived at the beginning of the barley harvest.
life.source: Ruth 1:19-22 (BSB).

life.text: Ruth gleaned in Boaz's field; he asked whose young woman she was, told her to stay with his servant girls and drink from the young men's jars, gave her roasted grain, told his men to pull stalks from the bundles for her; she gleaned about an ephah of barley and brought Naomi the food she had saved.
life.source: Ruth 2:1-18 (BSB).

life.text: Naomi sent Ruth, washed and perfumed, to the threshing floor; at midnight Boaz found her at his feet; she asked him to spread his garment over her as kinsman-redeemer; he promised to redeem if the nearer kinsman would not; he gave her six measures of barley before dawn.
life.source: Ruth 3 (BSB).
life.note: The myth entry sets Ezekiel 16:8 ('I spread My cloak over you ... you became Mine') beside Ruth 3:9 as 'the same picture'. The BSB's English words differ; the page says 'picture', not 'words'.

life.text: At the town gate, before ten elders, the nearer kinsman gave up the right of redemption because it would jeopardize his inheritance, and removed his sandal; the elders blessed the marriage (Rachel and Leah).
life.source: Ruth 4:1-12 (BSB). Ruth 4:7 calls the sandal custom that of 'former times in Israel'.

life.text: Ruth bore Obed; the neighbour women named him; he was the father of Jesse, the father of David.
life.source: Ruth 4:13-17 (BSB).

life.text: Outside her book, only Matthew 1:5 names her; Matthew's genealogy names five women (Tamar 1:3, Rahab and Ruth 1:5, Uriah's wife 1:6, Mary 1:16), and gives Rahab as the mother of Boaz.
life.source: BSB searched for 'Ruth' (86 lines; the only one outside the book of Ruth is Matthew 1:5).

life.text: 'Ruth the Moabitess' five times in her book (1:22; 2:2; 2:21; 4:5; 4:10).
life.source: BSB search.
life.note: The foreman also calls her 'the Moabitess' at 2:6.

life.text: Her parents are mentioned but not named.
life.source: Ruth 2:11 (BSB): 'how you left your father and mother and the land of your birth'.

life.text: Her name: Hebrew Rut, probably from a word for friendship.
life.source: Bible Hub, Strong's Hebrew 7327: 'Probably for r'uwth; friend'; NAS Exhaustive Concordance: '"friendship," a Moabite ancestress of David'; BDB: 'for רְעוּת, i.e. friendship'.

life.text: Christian Bibles place the book after Judges, following the Septuagint; the Hebrew Bible places it among the Writings (Ketubim), the second of the Five Megillot.
life.source: Catholic Encyclopedia (1912), 'Book of Ruth', Place in the canon; Jewish Encyclopedia (1906), 'Ruth, Book of': 'In the Hebrew Bible, however, Ruth is found in the "Ketubim," or third part of the canon, where it stands next after the Song of Solomon, being the second of the Five Megillot.'

life.text: An ancient Beraitha in the Talmud (Baba Bathra) says Samuel wrote Judges and Ruth; the Catholic Encyclopedia calls the ascription groundless; the author is unknown.
life.source: Catholic Encyclopedia (1912), 'Book of Ruth', Author and date: '"Samuel wrote his book, Judges, and Ruth"; but this ascription of Ruth to Samuel is groundless and hence almost universally rejected at the present day. The name of the author of the book of Ruth is unknown'.

life.text: Josephus sets the story under Eli's government, and has Boaz bid Ruth loose the kinsman's shoe and spit in his face 'according to the law'; the book has the kinsman remove his own sandal (Ruth 4:8), while Deuteronomy 25:9 prescribes the widow's removing the sandal and spitting.
life.source: Josephus, Antiquities 5.9.1 and 5.9.4 (Whiston), people/ruth/josephus-antiquities-5.txt; Ruth 4:8; Deuteronomy 25:9 (BSB).
life.note: Antiquities is dated to about 93-94; the page says 'around the year 93'.

life.text: Jews read the book of Ruth at Shavuot, the Feast of Weeks, 50 days after Passover.
life.source: Britannica, 'Ruth' (biblical figure): 'Ruth's story is celebrated during the Jewish festival of Shavuot, the Feast of Weeks, 50 days after Passover.' Britannica, 'Shavuot': 'Customs during Shavuot include ... reading the Book of Ruth'; 'Some rabbis interpret Ruth's experience with hardship and famine in connection with the agricultural holiday'.

life.text: Deuteronomy 23:3 bars Moabites from the assembly of the LORD 'even to the tenth generation'; Ruth the Moabitess was David's great-grandmother.
life.source: Deuteronomy 23:3; Ruth 4:17 (BSB). The Catholic Encyclopedia (1912) notes the same tension under 'Purpose'.
life.note: The page states both verses side by side and draws no conclusion. The rabbinic reading ('a Moabite, not a Moabitess', Mishnah Yevamot 8:3) was not fetched in a public-domain text and is left out.

life.text: When Saul hunted him, David asked the king of Moab to shelter his father and mother.
life.source: 1 Samuel 22:3-4 (BSB).
life.note: The page does not say why he chose Moab.

life.text: In the 1880s the traditional tomb of Jesse was shown with that of Ruth in a small mosque in the Deir el Arbain at Hebron.
life.source: C. R. Conder and H. H. Kitchener, The Survey of Western Palestine, Memoirs vol. 3 (1883), p. 308 and the Deir el Arbain entry: 'The tomb of Jesse (Kabr Yessa) is shown with that of Ruth in a small mosque, with a Mihrab in one corner, in this building.' people/ruth/survey-western-palestine-3.txt.
life.note: Wikipedia cites Quaresmius (1639) for an earlier report; not fetched, so the page gives only the 1883 survey.

life.text: The Keats lines: 'the self-same song that found a path / Through the sad heart of Ruth, when, sick for home, / She stood in tears amid the alien corn'.
life.source: John Keats, Ode to a Nightingale, in Lamia, Isabella, The Eve of St. Agnes, and Other Poems (1820); Project Gutenberg ebook 23684, people/ruth/keats-poems-1820.txt.
life.note: The ode was written in 1819. The book of Ruth has her weep only in Moab (1:9, 1:14).

fathers.text: Chrysostom: Matthew names Ruth and Rahab 'the one an alien, the other an harlot'; Boaz 'neither despised her poverty nor abhorred her mean birth', a picture of Christ and the Church; she 'became a mother of kings'.
fathers.source: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 3 (NPNF 1/10), shared/npnf110.txt.

fathers.text: Ambrose: 'a Ruth will never be wanting who will prefer the widowed life of her mother-in-law to her father's house', to mothers-in-law who instruct well.
fathers.note: Ambrose also reads the sandal at the gate as a figure of Christ the Bridegroom (Exposition of the Christian Faith, book 3, chapter 10); read, not used.

fathers.text: Jerome to Paula: 'Ruth, a stranger, never left her side. And see what a great thing it is to comfort a lonely woman! Ruth, for her reward, is made an ancestress of Christ.'
fathers.source: Jerome, Letter 39 (to Paula, on Blaesilla's death), section 5 (NPNF 2/6), people/ruth/npnf206.txt.
fathers.note: Jerome's Letter 108 has Paula, dead at Bethlehem, say to 'the true Naomi' Ruth's words; read, not used.

fathers.text: Josephus: 'I was therefore obliged to relate this history of Ruth, because I had a mind to demonstrate the power of God ...'
fathers.note: Capitals for God applied (Who, He); verify-quotes ignores case.

feasts.text: OCA: Righteous Ruth, 'the wife of Boaz', commemorated on the Sunday of the Forefathers (the Sunday between 11 and 17 December; 13 December in 2026).
feasts.source: OCA lives, 2026-12-13, '615-righteous-ruth' ('Righteous Ruth ... Information about the Righteous Ruth, the wife of Boaz, may be found in the Old Testament book bearing her name') and '80-sunday-of-the-forefathers' ('The Sunday that falls between December 11-17 is known as the Sunday of the Holy Forefathers').
feasts.note: A movable Sunday, so the feasts grid carries no East date; the note says it in words.

feasts.text: OCA: the Sunday before the Nativity names 'the righteous Ruth, wife of Boaz' among the righteous women of the Old Testament.
No day for Ruth in the Roman Martyrology (1916), the Calendarium Romanum (1969), the USCCB 2026 calendar, the Church of England calendar, Lesser Feasts and Fasts 2022 or the ELCA church year.
feasts.source: Searched shared/martyrology-1916.txt, calendarium-romanum-1969-ocr.txt, usccb-2026cal.txt, cofe-calendar.txt, lff2022.txt (its 'Ruth' is one of the Martyrs of Memphis, 9 September), elca-churchyear.txt (lectionary readings only).
feasts.note: The 2004 Martyrologium Romanum was not checked; the page speaks only of 'the Catholic calendar' used at Mass and the 1916 martyrology.

pictures.what: Ruth swearing her allegiance to Naomi, Jan Victors, 1653, oil on canvas, 108.6 x 137.2 cm; signed and dated upper right; sold at Sotheby's New York 2015 (pendant to a painting in the Lazienki Palace on the Water, Warsaw).
pictures.size: original 2000 x 1611; saved 1800 x 1450 (light 0.5 px blur against canvas grain), 336 KB
pictures.note: Ruth, right, in a woven red and gold hat, hand on heart; Naomi seated, left. Faces at about 67% / 22% (Ruth) and 47% / 30% (Naomi).

pictures.what: Ruth in Boaz's Field, Julius Schnorr von Carolsfeld, 1828, oil on canvas, 59 x 70 cm, the National Gallery, London (NG6570, bought 1997). Detail: Ruth with the reapers.
pictures.note: A Commons featured picture. Boaz, left of the full painting, is cut from the detail; the caption says 'a detail'.

pictures.size: 826 x 1322 as on Commons (no larger copy), 212 KB
pictures.note: Gallery picture (wide screens only), added because the pictures column ended 671 px above the facts.

rejected_pictures: Francesco Hayez, Ruth (1853, Bologna) and A woman as Ruth (1835): partly unclothed; not right for this site.
Philip Hermogenes Calderon, Ruth and Naomi (1886): the Walker copy is 1000 x 810; the Yale CC0 file is a print with its margins and title.
Jacob Pynas and Pieter Lastman: small figures in a landscape.
William Blake, Naomi entreating Ruth and Orpah (1795): 1024 px, and the colour print is pale.
could_not_verify: Rabbinic legends (Ruth a daughter of King Eglon, in Ruth Rabbah; that she lived to see Solomon): no public-domain text fetched; left out.
The rabbinic reading of Deuteronomy 23:3 as 'a Moabite, not a Moabitess' (Mishnah Yevamot 8:3): no public-domain translation fetched; left out.
Quaresmius (1639) on the Hebron tomb: not fetched; the page cites only the 1883 survey.
The 2004 Roman Martyrology: not checked for Ruth.
That the book is often read at weddings (myth 1): common knowledge, not sourced.

checked: Every number: 7 sons (Ruth 4:15), the 5 women of Matthew 1, about ten years (1:4), an ephah (2:17), six measures (3:15), ten elders (4:2), 'Ruth the Moabitess' five times; Deuteronomy 23:3 word for word in the BSB.

Feasts: 16 July in shared/lsb-calendar.txt; the OCA's Sunday of the Forefathers 'between December 11-17' (people/ruth/oca-forefathers.txt); no day in the Catholic, Anglican or Episcopal calendars on disk.

Attributions against the texts on disk: Josephus has Boaz bid Ruth 'loose his shoe, and spit in his face, according to the law' and sets the story under Eli (Whiston); Chrysostom's Homily 3 on Matthew reads Boaz and Ruth as Christ and the Church (npnf110); Ambrose, Concerning Widows; Jerome, Letter 39; Keats's lines and the 1819 date; the Catholic Encyclopedia calling the Talmud's ascription to Samuel groundless.
Myths: each truth rests on the text; the threshing-floor entry picks no winner.

Rules: capitals for God in every quotation and in our text; never 'St Ruth'; plain sentences; no section marks; number tiles natural; band not violent; licences as the Commons pages give them; verify-quotes exits 0; saints-test passes.
